- ("http","example.com","80","/","","")  -> lines: http / example.com / 80 / "/" / "" / "" / "http://example.com:80/" / 1

- Case: "HTTP", "Http", "HtTpS" -> is it lowercased?
- Whitespace: " http", "http ", " http ", "ht tp", "\thttp", "http\n" (use $'\t' / $'\n' in bash) -> trimmed? preserved?
- Trailing colon / separator: "http:", "http://", "://" -> stripped?
- Non-alpha: "1http", "+http", "ht_tp", "ht-tp", "ht.tp", "ht+tp", "HTTP2", "" -> stored verbatim?
- Unicode/UTF-8 multibyte: "htTPÜ", "日本" -> byte-preserved? any case mapping applied to non-ASCII bytes (watch for locale-dependent tolower on bytes >= 0x80)?

rules.rule: scheme is transformed by a pure per-byte ASCII lowercase map and nothing else: for each byte b in the input string, out_b = (0x41 <= b <= 0x5A) ? b + 0x20 : b. Exhaustive single-byte sweep over all 254 testable byte values (0x01-0xFF, excluding 0x0A which was tested separately) shows exactly bytes 0x41..0x5A are remapped to 0x61..0x7A and every other byte is identical.
The transform is byte-identical to `LC_ALL=C tr 'A-Z' 'a-z'` for arbitrary multi-byte input: length-preserving, order-preserving, no dedup, no insertion/removal of any byte.
rules.evidence: 16-string corpus compared byte-for-byte against LC_ALL=C tr output, all OK, any_diff=0. e.g. in=4d695865442d436153652e3132332b58 ("MiXeD-CaSe.123+X") -> got=6d697865642d636173652e3132332b78 == exp_ascii_tolower; in=413a422f433f442345 ("A:B/C?D#E") -> got=613a622f633f642365

rules.rule: NO whitespace trimming is performed. Leading and trailing spaces are preserved exactly (and are then emitted into to_string, producing a malformed URL).
rules.evidence: (" http","example.com","80","/","","") -> line1 " http", line7 " http://example.com:80/"; ("http ",...) -> line1 "http ", line7 "http ://example.com:80/"; ("   HTTP   ",...) -> line1 "   http   ", line7 "   http   ://example.com:80/"; ("  ","example.com","80","/","","") -> line1 "  ", line7 "  ://example.com:80/", is_valid=1

rules.evidence: ("ht tp","example.com","80","/","","") -> line1 "ht tp", line7 "ht tp://example.com:80/"; ("HT TP",...) -> line1 "ht tp"

rules.rule: All ASCII control characters are stored verbatim: TAB(0x09), LF(0x0A), CR(0x0D), VT(0x0B), FF(0x0C), 0x01, DEL(0x7F). They are neither stripped nor trimmed, and are re-emitted in to_string.

rules.rule: No trailing separator stripping: a trailing ':' , '//' or '://' in the scheme argument is NOT removed. to_string then emits the stored scheme followed by its own literal "://", producing doubled separators.

rules.rule: No scheme syntax validation or rejection: schemes starting with a digit or non-alpha, and schemes containing '_', '-', '.', '+', '%', '@', '[', ']', '{', '}', '\\', '^', '`', '|', '~', ':' or '/' are all stored verbatim (modulo ASCII lowercase), and is_valid() is unaffected (still 1 for the standard host/path combo).

uncertainties: Cannot distinguish the implementation idiom: `std::transform(s.begin(), s.end(), s.begin(), [](unsigned char c){ return std::tolower(c); })` (with a correct unsigned-char cast, C locale) is behaviorally IDENTICAL to a hand-rolled `if (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') c += 32;`. Both match every one of the 254 observed byte mappings. The binary evidently never calls setlocale(LC_ALL, "") / imbues a non-C locale, since 6 different LC_ALL/LANG settings produced identical maps — so the ambiguity is unresolvable by black-box observation.

Embedded NUL bytes in the scheme cannot be tested: execve/argv terminates the string at the first 0x00, so $'HT\x00TP' reached the program as just "HT". Whether from_components would preserve an interior NUL in a std::string is unobservable through this CLI.

No upper bound on scheme length was found (100000 bytes stored intact); a limit may exist above that but was not probed, nor was allocation-failure behavior.

This dimension only observed that is_valid() stays 1 for arbitrary garbage schemes when host+path are well-formed, and that scheme="" collapses the whole scheme://authority prefix. Whether the *value* of a non-empty scheme feeds any other logic (e.g. default-port selection, scheme-specific validation, is_valid rules) was not exhaustively explored — that belongs to the port/validity dimensions. Note ("http",...,"80",...) keeps :80 in to_string, so no http/80 default-port suppression was seen.

The `stoi` abort on non-numeric port (exit 134, std::invalid_argument) happens before any output, which means no scheme case can be tested with a non-numeric port argument. All scheme conclusions are therefore conditioned on a parseable integer port.
